analysis.title: US CPI preview: upside pressures building
key_insights: ANZ forecasts October headline CPI +0.3% m/m and core CPI +0.3% m/m. If in line, imputed 12-month rates would rise to 4.0% y/y headline and 2.9% y/y core, which ANZ reads as inflation momentum re-accelerating.
BLS will not publish y/y inflation rates for October 2026 because October 2025 data are unavailable after last year's federal government shutdown. The y/y figures are ANZ's imputed estimates.

At the October post-FOMC press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said inflation remains elevated and risks to the outlook are skewed to the upside. He stressed that relative price changes in some sectors must not broaden across the economy and that inflation expectations must stay anchored.

ISM price indices, the NFIB small business survey and the S&P Global PMI show businesses facing steep cost pressures from transportation, raw materials and interest costs. With strong new orders and production, ANZ sees further pipeline inflation.

The FOMC held rates in October to assess data over 'information-rich intervals'. ANZ believes re-accelerating inflation and robust demand make further hikes inevitable, and expects a 25bp hike in December and another 25bp in March 2027.
ANZ says the summer disinflation trend has stalled. Inflation data over the last two months suggest momentum is rising, and much of the rise in headline inflation so far has come from supply shocks.

Supercore CPI momentum on a six-month moving-average basis has accelerated since August. Supercore services momentum has picked up, which ANZ reads as price pressures firming beyond the direct effect of higher energy prices.
Six-month and 12-month annualised rates of market-based core PCE rose in September.
ANZ asks whether demand-pull inflation is starting to emerge, and says the FOMC will focus on whether pressures are still cost-push or becoming demand-pull.

Medium-term inflation expectations are around 3.5%, above the Fed's 2% target. ANZ warns elevated near-term surveyed expectations could de-anchor medium-term expectations, and says policy needs to lean against that risk.

Chart headlines flag higher gasoline prices as an upside risk, core goods inflation momentum picking up with used cars and apparel accelerating, broad-based supercore inflation, and shelter prices picking up again. The text gives no figures for these charts.

Longer-term market-implied inflation expectations remain relatively well anchored, while surveyed expectations have risen, especially near-term. NY Fed long-term expectations are steady but medium- and near-term expectations have edged up.

tension_points.bull_case: Much of the rise in headline inflation has come from supply shocks, which means pressure is cost-push rather than demand-driven.
tension_points.bear_case: Supercore momentum, core goods and shelter are firming, and strong new orders and production show demand holding up. ANZ sees nascent signs of demand-pull inflation and expects hikes in December and March.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The FOMC is assessing whether pressures are primarily cost-push or demand-pull. ANZ's hike call rests on a re-acceleration in inflation alongside robust demand, so core CPI running below ANZ's 0.3% m/m forecast would weaken it.

theme_stances.key_argument: Re-accelerating inflation alongside robust demand means further rate rises are inevitable.
The summer disinflation trend proved fleeting and supercore, core goods and shelter pressures are firming.
theme_stances.evidence: The underlying disinflation trend evident over the summer months proved fleeting.
